title: Questhand 101
subtitle: How to use Questhand, made in Questhand

lessons.title: Welcome to Questhand
lessons.goal: Know what a card, a lesson and the Map are

modules.title: A course is a deck of cards
modules.body:
Each lesson is a short row of cards. A card is one small thing to do: read, watch, answer, make or discuss.

Your students play one card at a time and always see what comes next. You see every card at once, on the **Map**.

This course is made in Questhand, so you'll learn it the way your students will. Work through the cards in order.

modules.title: Where are you starting from?
modules.body: There's no wrong answer. It only changes which card you get next.

questions.text: How much have you used online course tools?
options: Never, this is new to me

modules.title: New here? Two words are enough
modules.body:
**Card**: one small thing for a student to do.

**Lesson**: a row of cards, played in order.

That's all you need to start. Everything else in this course is a way to make cards do more.

modules.title: Coming from another tool?
modules.body:
Two things work differently here.

1. **Everything is a card.** A lesson is quick to build and easy to change: drag cards on the Map to rearrange them.
2. **Answers deal cards.** What a student gets next can depend on what they just answered. No rules to set up: you draw a line from the answer to the card.

modules.title: What your students see
modules.body:
Students open a course to **Today**: the one card to play now, big, with today's lesson under it. Small tags beside it say what else needs them: a card to revise, one overdue or due soon, or an elective to choose.

- **All cards** shows every week, with the cards they've done face up.
- **My board** keeps their own work in one place.

On the Map you see each card the way students see its face.

questions.text: Where do you see every card of the course at once?
questions.explain: The Map shows each lesson as a row of cards, with lines from answers to the cards they deal.

lessons.title: Cards, the building blocks
lessons.goal: Make a Content card and a Question card

modules.title: Two kinds of card
modules.body:
**Content** cards hold something to read, watch or listen to.

**Question** cards ask something back. Under **How students answer**, pick one of four:

- **Choices**: with a right answer, or a poll with none.
- **Open answer**: students hand in words, a drawing, a recording or a file.
- **Worksheet**: they fill in the page you wrote.
- **Discussion**: a feed of posts and replies.

modules.title: Make a card
modules.body:
On the Map, press **+ Card** on a lesson's row and pick **Content** or **Question**. The card's panel opens on the right: give it a title and what students should do.

Everything saves as you type. Close the panel (or press Esc) and the card is on the map, its face already showing what's in it.

modules.title: Card quiz
modules.body: Three quick questions. Your score decides which card you get next.

questions.text: You want students to watch a short video. Which card?
questions.explain: A Content card holds words, pictures, videos, links and recordings.

questions.text: Students should vote, and no answer is right. Which card?
options: Choices, with Has a right answer: No
questions.explain: A poll is a Choices card with no right answer. After voting, students see how the class voted.

questions.text: A student should write a paragraph or upload a photo of their work. Which card?
questions.explain: An Open answer card takes words, a drawing, a recording or a file.

modules.title: The card kinds, side by side
modules.body:
- **Content**: something to read, watch or listen to.
- **Choices with a right answer**: checked at once. One answer, several, an order, or a short typed answer.
- **Choices with no right answer**: a poll.
- **Open answer**: students hand in work, and you give feedback.
- **Worksheet**: a page to fill in, alone, in a group or as a class.
- **Discussion**: posts and replies.

You got this card because of your quiz score. Students who scored higher went straight on.

modules.title: Ahead of the class: card groups
modules.body:
Full marks. The quiz you just took was a **card group**: several cards answered together, with one score.

To make one, drag a box around cards on the Map (start on an empty spot) and press **Make a card group**. Under the group, its score ranges can each deal a card, just like an answer. That's how this card reached you.

modules.title: Your turn: plan a card
modules.body:
Think of a lesson you'll teach soon. Which card would you open it with, and why? Write a few lines, or record yourself saying it.

This card has Allow AI feedback ticked: once a teacher connects their AI, students get a few lines back the moment they hand in.

lessons.title: Every kind of question
lessons.goal: Pick the right kind of question

modules.title: Five ways to ask
modules.body:
A Choices card can ask in five ways. With **Has a right answer: Yes**, pick **One answer**, **Several**, **Order** or **Short answer**. With **No (a poll)**, it's a vote.

Try three of them on the next cards. Each student sees the options in their own order, so the right one isn't always first.

questions.text: What can a Content card hold? Choose all that apply.
questions.explain: Grades come from Question cards. Content cards hold things to read, watch or listen to.

questions.text: Put the steps of making a branch in order.
options: Drag an answer's dot to a card
questions.explain: Question, answers, then drag each answer to the card it deals, and check it as a student.

questions.text: Which tab shows every card of the course at once? (one word)
questions.explain: The Map. Short answers ignore capitals, spaces and punctuation.

modules.title: Math in a card
modules.body:
Write math between dollar signs and students see it typeset: $\frac{3}{4} + \frac{1}{8} = \frac{7}{8}$, or $x^2 + y^2 = r^2$.

It works in a card's text, its questions, its options and the explanation.

modules.title: How is it going?
modules.body: Pick one and press Submit vote.

questions.text: How do you feel about building your first course?

modules.title: More help, just for you
modules.body:
You said you need more help, so this card is yours. No one else sees it.

Start small: one lesson, three cards. Something to read, one question, and one card that an answer deals. Then open **Student View** and play it as a student.

modules.title: Several questions, one card group
modules.body:
Writing a quiz? On a Choices card, press **+ Add the next question**. Each question goes on its own card, and the cards become a card group: answered together, with one score.

One question per card keeps the tree simple: each answer can deal its own card.

weeks.title: Week 2 · Card trees and your course

lessons.title: Card trees
lessons.goal: Deal a card from an answer and from a score

modules.title: Why branch?
modules.body:
A class doesn't all need the same next step. Some need another example; some are ready for a challenge.

On the Map, each line runs from an answer to the card it deals. Students who pick that answer get the card. The others never see it.

modules.title: Draw a branch
modules.body:
Every answer on a Question card has a small dot on the Map. Drag the dot to empty space and pick the kind of card it deals, or drop it on a card that's already there.

One answer can deal more than one card: drag its dot again.

modules.title: Try a branch
modules.body: This card is a branch itself: each answer deals a different card.

questions.text: A student answers “I'm not sure yet”. What should they get next?
options: Another example, explained step by step
questions.explain: A short extra example, only for the students who need it, is what a branch is for.

modules.title: Yes: a short extra example
modules.body: That's the idea. Make the extra example a small card, and drag the “not sure” answer to it. Only those students get it.

modules.title: Why not the same card again?
modules.body: Showing the same card rarely helps. Give a different way in instead: another example, a video, a picture.

modules.title: Why not just move on?
modules.body: A student who isn't sure yet will likely be stuck on the next card too. A short detour card helps them catch up first.

modules.title: Branch by score
modules.body:
A card group can deal cards by score. Its score ranges sit under it on the Map, such as 0–59%, 60–99% and 100%. Drag a range's dot to the card it deals, just like an answer.

Scores count the student's best try, so a better retake deals the better card.

attachments.name: A card group and its score ranges

modules.title: Deal a card in a later lesson
modules.body:
An answer can deal a card in another lesson. When you make the card from the answer's dot, pick the lesson under **New card in**.

The student gets the card when they reach that lesson, with a note saying which answer opened it.

modules.title: Who gets a card
modules.body:
A card's panel says who gets it, under **Access**:

- **Everyone gets this card**: the usual.
- **Students get it from** an answer or a score: set on the Map, by drawing the line.
- **Only some students or groups**: pick them by name.

modules.title: Sketch your own tree
modules.body: Draw a small tree for one of your lessons: one question, its answers, and the card each answer deals. Press **Draw**, or describe it in words.

modules.title: This card waited for you
modules.body:
In the first lesson you said online course tools are new to you. That answer dealt this card, here, in a later lesson: a card can wait until a student reaches it.

For your first tree, keep it tiny: one question with two answers, and one extra card for the answer that needs help. That's a whole branch.

lessons.title: Building your course
lessons.goal: Set up a course: weeks, dates, a cover

modules.title: Make a course
modules.body:
On your courses page, press **New course**. Give it a name (a subtitle is optional), then choose:

- **Start blank**: one empty week to fill yourself.
- **Standard weeks**: three weeks with a ready-made rhythm of goal, example, quick check, task, discussion and reflection.
- **From a course file**: a course someone exported from Questhand.

modules.title: A cover for your course
modules.body:
Every course has a cover from the start: a paper-cut scene that fits its name, in its own colour. Your students see it on their courses page.

To change it, open **Settings → Course**. Pick one of four paper covers (with your AI connected, it picks them from what the course teaches), search open photos, draw one with a Google AI key, or **Upload** your own.

modules.title: Weeks and lessons
modules.body:
Each lesson is a row on the Map, and lessons sit in weeks.

- **+ Card** on a lesson's row adds a card.
- **+ Lesson in Week 1** (under the week) adds a lesson; **+ Week 2** adds a week.
- Click a lesson's name to rename it.
- A lesson's **⋯** menu holds the rest: move, copy, save, delete.

modules.title: Dates and today's lesson
modules.body:
Each lesson can have a date. The lesson for today is the one on top of every student's Today.

To date them all at once, open a lesson's **⋯** menu and pick **Schedule lessons from here**: choose the first class and the days you meet.

No dates? Pick a lesson's **⋯ → Make it today's lesson** when the class moves on.

modules.title: Use a card again
modules.body:
Made a card you'll want again, like a weekly reflection? Press **Collect** at the top of its panel. It's in **Saved cards** the next time you press **+ Card**, in any course.

A whole lesson can be saved the same way, from its **⋯** menu.

modules.title: Already have a plan written?
modules.body:
**Settings → Files → Import from a document…**: upload your course plan, look over the weeks and cards Questhand proposes, untick what you don't want, and add them.

The same place exports a course: **Questhand (.json)** to keep a copy or share it, or **Canvas / Moodle** for another system.

questions.text: Your lessons have no dates, and the class is moving on to lesson 3. What do you do?
options: Nothing: students move on by themselves
Lesson 3's ⋯ menu → Make it today's lesson
questions.explain: Today's lesson is the one on top of every student's Today. Without dates, you choose it.

lessons.title: Working on the map
lessons.goal: Find, move and undo on the Map

modules.title: Getting around the map
modules.body:
Scroll to move around, and zoom with the buttons at the bottom left (or pinch). Point at the map's left edge to see every week and lesson; click one to go there.

Press **/** to search: type any word on a card and pick a result to jump to it.

modules.title: Move, pick and tidy
modules.body:
- **Move a card**: drag it along its row, or into another lesson.
- **Pick several**: drag a box around them, starting on an empty spot. Then move them together, delete them, or make them a card group.
- **Deleted something?** The trash button at the bottom of the map puts it back.

modules.title: One undo for everything
modules.body:
Everything saves as you go: you'll see **Saved** at the top right.

**Undo** (⌘Z or Ctrl+Z) and **Redo** sit at the top of the page and of every card's panel: one undo for every change, on the Map or in a card. The clock beside them is **History**: every change, to step back to.

modules.title: Keyboard shortcuts
modules.body:
Press **?** on any page for the full list. The ones you'll use most:

- **1**, **2**, **3**: Map, Students, Settings.
- **n**: a new card.
- **/**: find a card.
- In a card's panel, **[** and **]** go to the previous and next card.
- On the Map, the arrow keys move between cards and Enter opens one.

questions.text: Put the steps of making a card group and branching from its score in order.
options: Drag a box around the cards
Drag a score range's dot to a card
questions.explain: Pick the cards, make the group, wire its score ranges, then try it as a student.

modules.title: Format a card
modules.body:
## Text that's easy to read

A card can have **headings**, *emphasis*, lists, links and tables. Use the bar above the text, or type: **⌘B** for bold, a line starting with - for a list.

> A callout like this one is good for a tip.

| Kind | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| Content | Read, watch, listen |
| Question | Ask something back |

modules.title: Worksheets
modules.body:
When students should fill something in, make a Question card and pick **Worksheet** under How students answer. Your text is the worksheet: headings, prompts, a table with empty cells.

**Who fills it in**:

- **Each student**: everyone gets their own copy.
- **Each group**: a group shares one copy and writes in it together, live.
- **Whole class**: one copy for everyone.

modules.title: Try it: plan a lesson in your own copy
modules.body:
## My first lesson

**Topic:** 

**By the end, students can:** 

| Card | What students do |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | |
| 2 | |
| 3 | |

**The question that branches, and what each answer deals:**

modules.title: Media on a card
modules.body:
Under a card's text: **Link**, **Upload**, **Draw**, and **Record** (audio, video, your screen or a photo, right in the browser).

- A video can play just one part: set where it starts and stops.
- **Make cover** puts a picture on the card's face.
- Students hand in work with the same buttons.

modules.title: Record a hello
modules.body: Record a short hello for your future class: who you are, and what the first lesson is about. Press **Record** for your voice or a video, or write it instead.

modules.title: AI feedback on handed-in work
modules.body:
Connect your own AI account once, in your account's **Settings → Tools for cards** (Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini, with your own key). Then tick **Allow AI feedback** on any Open answer card.

When a student hands in, they get a few lines of feedback right away: what works, one thing to try next. You see it too, beside their work, and your own feedback still counts most.

lessons.title: Groups and discussions
lessons.goal: Run group work and a discussion

modules.title: Writing together
modules.body:
With a worksheet for **Each group**, every group shares one copy and sees each other typing. Make the groups right on the card: name them, split the class at random, or tap students into each group.

Groups are kept in **Students → Class list and groups**, so other cards can use them.

modules.title: Let students pick their group
modules.body:
Sometimes students should choose: a project, a topic, a time. Make a poll and tick **Make groups from the answers**. Each option becomes a group, and students can switch until you lock the groups.

Try it on the next card.

modules.title: Pick your study group
modules.body: Choose the group you'll work with for the rest of the course. The next worksheet is shared with your group.

questions.text: Which group do you want to join?

modules.title: Our group's first lesson
modules.body:
Fill this in together: everyone in your group writes in the same copy, live.

**Topic:** 


| Card | Kind     | What students do |
| ---- | -------- | ---------------- |
| 1    | Content  |                  |
| 2    | Question |                  |
| 3    |          |                  |


**Who builds which card:**

modules.title: Just exploring? Start here
modules.body:
You picked **Just exploring**, so this card is yours.

Take one lesson you already teach and turn just its first ten minutes into three cards: something to read or watch, one question, and one card an answer deals.

modules.title: Our class in numbers
modules.body:
## How long did this course take you?

Add a row with your name and about how many minutes you've spent on Questhand 101 so far. Everyone writes in this one table.

| Name | Minutes |
| --- | --- |
| Example | 40 |

modules.title: Setting up a discussion
modules.body:
A Discussion card is a feed of posts, each with its replies.

- Posts are written like a card: formatting, math, and Record, Upload, Draw or Link.
- You choose who posts, whether students reply and react, and whether posts wait for your approval.
- Ask for replies, such as “reply to two classmates”, and the card is done when they have.

modules.title: Introduce yourself
modules.body: Post a line about you and what you teach. Then reply to one classmate; try a voice reply with Record.

modules.title: Peer review: your lesson plan
modules.body:
Post your lesson plan: a few lines, a photo of a sketch, or the worksheet you filled in. Then give feedback on two plans.

Each reply has three parts: **what I noticed**, **the effect it had on me**, and **one thing to try next**.

modules.title: Why an elective?
modules.body:
An elective is a lesson students choose to take. Make one from a lesson's **⋯** menu. Students see it in its week with its cards face down, and press **Choose**.

Once a course has electives, **Settings → Class** says how many each student should take.

modules.title: Reading pack
modules.body: Three short readings that go together. A card group can hold any kind of card, not only questions.

modules.title: Reading 1: small cards
modules.body: Short cards are easier to start and easier to finish. Students see progress after every card.

modules.title: Reading 2: one question per card
modules.body: One question per card keeps the tree simple: each answer deals its own next card.

modules.title: Reading 3: feedback that moves
modules.body: Feedback helps most with one thing done well and one thing to try next.

lessons.title: Bringing students in
lessons.goal: Invite a class and manage who joins

modules.title: Invite your class
modules.body:
Press **Invite students** (on the Map, or in the Students tab). Then:

1. **By email**: type their addresses, and each gets their own link.
2. **The class code or link**: share it, or show the QR code in class.

Every student signs in with their own account (Google, or email and password).

modules.title: Who can join
modules.body:
In the invite box, **General access** decides what the class code and link do:

- **Restricted**: only students you invite.
- **Anyone with the link or code, after you let them in**: they wait until you press **Let in**.
- **Anyone with the link or code**: they join straight away.

Add a **Join passcode** for one more step, or make a **New code** if the old one got out.

modules.title: Your class list
modules.body:
**Students → Class list and groups** lists everyone, with a way to message them, send their link again, or remove them. Their work stays saved.

The groups made on cards are there too, to rename or change.

modules.title: Demo students
modules.body:
Demo students are made-up students on your class list, for you to try the course as. In **Students → Class list and groups**, press **Add a demo student**. What you do as them is kept, like a real student's, so groups, discussions and the Students tab fill up.

They never get email, and once real students join, class numbers leave them out.

modules.title: Messages
modules.body:
Every conversation is in your **Inbox**, at the top right of a course. Its number counts new messages and new class activity together.

Students can always message you. Whether they can message each other is up to you, in **Settings → Class**.

questions.text: A student says: “I entered the class code, and it says I'm waiting.” What's going on?
options: Joining is set to “after you let them in”: press Let in
questions.explain: With that setting, people who use the code wait for you. You'll see them at the top of the Map and in Students.

lessons.title: Running your class
lessons.goal: See who needs you and give feedback

modules.title: Try it as a student
modules.body: **Student View**, at the top of every course, shows exactly what a student sees. Play as a demo student and your work is kept; as a new student it's only a test, and **Start over** clears it. No one is graded or notified.

modules.title: Who needs you
modules.body:
The **Students** tab has your class on the left. Pick **Whole class** to see a lesson at a glance: who is **Overdue**, whose work is **Ready for your feedback**, **Low quiz scores**, who **Haven't started**, and who has **Stalled**. Press **Remind** to send a short note.

Pick one student to see everything of theirs.

modules.title: Give feedback
modules.body:
Work students hand in waits for you in **Students**. Open it, write what they did well and one thing to try next. You can record how you'd say it, attach a file, or **Rate skills**.

Then press **Looks good**, or **Ask to revise**: the student sees the card come back to them, and hands in again.

modules.title: Share one idea
modules.body: What will your first Questhand lesson be about? Post one idea, and reply to someone else's.

lessons.title: Wrap-up
lessons.goal: Check what you know, then build

modules.title: Final check
modules.body: Five questions, two tries. Your best try decides your last card.

questions.text: How does a student get a card that an answer deals?
questions.explain: The answer deals it: only students who pick it get the card.

questions.text: Can one answer deal more than one card?
options: Yes: drag its dot to each card
questions.explain: Drag the same answer's dot onto another card and a second line appears.

questions.text: Where do you try the course as a student, with nothing graded?
questions.explain: Student View, at the top of every course.

questions.text: A student handed in work. Where is it waiting?
options: In Students, ready for your feedback
Nowhere until they finish the course
questions.explain: Handed-in work waits in the Students tab.

options: One thing done well, one thing to try next

modules.title: Let's go over it
modules.body:
No problem. These are the five things to remember:

1. Answers deal cards; only students who pick an answer get its card.
2. One answer can deal several cards.
3. Student View is a safe test: nothing is graded.
4. Handed-in work waits in Students.
5. Feedback: one thing done well, one thing to try next.

modules.title: You're ready
modules.body: Full marks. Go and build your first lesson: one Content card, one question, and one branch. Your students will feel the difference.

modules.title: What will you build first?
modules.body: One or two sentences: the lesson you'll build first, and the branch you'll put in it.
